initial_plan.years: Calendar years from 2013 through the latest year represented in the file; whether boundary years are complete will be checked.

answerability.part: The data can show annual reported pedestrian death counts in Brooklyn, but cannot establish safety per amount walked or individual pedestrian risk because walking exposure and person-level records are not present.

metric: Annual number of reported pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn crashes.
denominator: No denominator; this is an annual count, not an exposure-adjusted rate.
population: Reported pedestrian deaths in police-reported crashes in Brooklyn in each calendar year; counts are crash-level totals, not deduplicated people.
years: Full calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive. Exclude 2026 because the file ends on June 11, 2026, so that year is partial.
data_check_decisions: Keep crashes with a recorded Brooklyn borough and a crash date in 2013-2025; exclude rows with missing/placeholder borough because their borough cannot be assigned. Exclude 2026 because its date span is incomplete. Keep all qualifying Brooklyn rows and sum the supplied pedestrian death counts; this outcome field has no missing values in any checked Brooklyn year.
plan_change: The initial plan ran from 2013 through the latest file year. After the data check, the endpoint was set to 2025 because 2026 is only recorded through June 11; all earlier years from 2013 through 2025 span a full calendar year.

data_check.crash_date: No missing crash dates in the file; 2013-2025 each have recorded dates spanning January 1 to December 31, while 2026 spans January 1 to June 11.
data_check.borough: Among 2,132,218 dated crashes in 2013-2025, 659,713 (about 30.9%) have missing or placeholder borough values; there are zero impossible nonmissing values and zero values in the checked placeholder/default categories. Such records cannot be assigned to Brooklyn and are excluded, along with crashes assigned to other boroughs.
data_check.outcomes: Among Brooklyn crashes in each year 2013-2025, zero rows have a missing pedestrian-death count; no rows are dropped or treated as zero for missing outcomes.
data_check.partial_year: 2026 has 9,700 Brooklyn crash rows through June 11 and is excluded rather than compared as a full year.

limitations: This is a count of reported pedestrian deaths in police-reported Brooklyn crashes, not an exposure-adjusted rate; it cannot establish safety per walking trip or distance, and the supplied crash totals do not identify unique people across crashes.
